title: Global investment rises 6% to $1.6 trillion, but development gains remain uneven
key_claim: Global FDI rose 6% to $1.6 trillion in 2025, but the rebound was concentrated in a few megaprojects and strategic sectors, and countries adopted a record 229 investment policy measures.
frame_summary: UNCTAD is arguing that the headline recovery in cross-border investment does not tell you what is being built, because the flows are concentrated in a handful of economies, sectors and transactions and are shaped by increasingly active state policy.
verbatim_quote: Global foreign direct investment rose 6% to $1.6 trillion in 2025, ending two years of decline, but the recovery remains narrow, fragile and uneven, according to the World Investment Report 2026 by UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD).
verbatim_list: Strategic sectors such as AI infrastructure, semiconductors, critical minerals and energy-transition technologies and services accounted for 44% of global greenfield project values in 2025, up from 16% in 2020.
In 2025, countries adopted a record 229 investment policy measures.
The recovery should also be interpreted with caution: headline FDI numbers do not always translate into new factories, infrastructure, jobs or technology transfer.
notes: Headline anchor for the scan. Quote provenance manually verified 12/08/2026 from the live page during the pre-composition fetch.

title: Más capital, menos proyectos: la paradoja de la inversión en América Latina
key_claim: FDI into Latin America and the Caribbean rose 14% in 2025 while the announced value of greenfield projects fell by roughly a third, with especially sharp falls in Mexico and Argentina.
frame_summary: UNCTAD is arguing that Latin America's stronger headline inflow figure conceals a weakening pipeline of future productive capacity, so the region is receiving capital without securing the plant, infrastructure and supplier development that capital is supposed to bring.
verbatim_quote: Si bien las entradas totales aumentaron, el valor de los proyectos de inversión en nuevas instalaciones anunciados cayó aproximadamente un tercio, hasta menos de 120.000 millones de dólares.
verbatim_list: En otras palabras, en 2025 entró más capital en la región, pero se comprometió menos capital a construir nuevos activos productivos.
notes: Non-English Tier 1 primary source, per the multi-language sourcing rule; Latin America is the clearest regional case of the signal. Quote provenance manually verified 12/08/2026 from the live page.

title: New Foreign Direct Investment in the United States, 2025
date_evidence: EMBARGOED UNTIL RELEASE AT 8:30 a.m. EDT, Wednesday, June 10, 2026
key_claim: Of $232.2 billion of new foreign direct investment in the United States in 2025, $218.4 billion went on acquiring existing businesses, $4.6 billion on establishing new ones and $9.2 billion on expanding existing foreign-owned operations.
frame_summary: BEA's official statistics show that the headline surge in new inward direct investment into the United States is overwhelmingly a transfer of ownership of assets that already exist rather than the creation of new productive capacity.
verbatim_quote: Acquisition expenditures in 2025 were $218.4 billion, expenditures to establish new U.S. businesses were $4.6 billion, and expenditures to expand existing foreign-owned businesses were $9.2 billion.
notes: The load-bearing quantification for the scan: the acquisition-versus-establishment split in official US statistics. Quote provenance manually verified 12/08/2026 from the live release.

publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (FEDS Notes)
title: Recent Developments in Foreign Direct Investment into the U.S.
date_evidence: Kallen, Cody (2026). "Recent Developments in Foreign Direct Investment into the U.S.," FEDS Notes. Washington: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, June 26, 2026
key_claim: Aggregate FDI into the United States was broadly resilient in 2025 with limited visible impact from tariffs or trade policy uncertainty, and the shift towards acquisitions reflects the AI investment boom and industry composition.
frame_summary: The Federal Reserve note argues that the move from greenfield to acquisitions is a composition and technology-cycle story rather than evidence of political risk repricing, which is the strongest available counter to a reversibility reading.
verbatim_quote: In aggregate, foreign direct investment into the U.S. appeared resilient in 2025, with limited visible impacts from tariffs or trade policy uncertainty.
notes: Counter-evidence source, used in the Counter-Argument box. Quote provenance manually verified 12/08/2026 from the live page.

title: Europe's investment landscape shifts as short-term global headwinds test FDI, but long-term confidence endures
key_claim: FDI projects into Europe fell 7% in 2025 with France down 17%, the UK down 14% and Germany down 10%, while AI, defence and low-carbon energy projects grew sharply and geopolitical tension became the most-cited investor risk.
frame_summary: EY is arguing that Europe is seeing a shift rather than a retreat, with capital narrowing into a few strategic sectors and cheaper locations while the traditional industrial project pipeline in the largest economies contracts.
verbatim_quote: Europe's top investment destinations saw FDI decline in 2025, with France down 17%, the UK down 14% and Germany down 10%.
notes: European leg of the signal, from EY's annual attractiveness survey. Quote provenance manually verified 12/08/2026 from the live page.

title: Chinese investment rises to 7-year high: Chinese FDI in Europe, 2025 Update
key_claim: Chinese FDI into the EU and UK rose 67% to EUR 16.8 billion in 2025 on an 89% rebound in acquisitions, while newly announced Chinese greenfield commitments fell to EUR 5.2 billion from EUR 16.9 billion in 2023.
frame_summary: MERICS and Rhodium Group are arguing that Chinese firms have pivoted away from building new European plant towards buying into existing companies and exporting into the market, reversing the greenfield-led pattern of the previous three years.
verbatim_quote: In 2025, just EUR 5.2 billion in new Chinese investments in plants and equipment were announced, down from EUR 5.7 billion in 2024 and a steep drop from EUR 16.9 billion in 2023.
notes: Co-published with Rhodium Group. Shows the same acquisition-over-construction pattern in a single investor country. Quote provenance manually verified 12/08/2026 from the live page.

title: Europe FDI dips 7% but tops 5,000 projects in 2025, says EY survey
key_claim: European FDI project numbers fell 7% in 2025 and FDI-linked job creation fell 25%, a smaller decline than the 16% fall in global industrial greenfield investment reported by UNCTAD.
frame_summary: Investment Monitor is arguing that Europe is outperforming a wider global contraction in new industrial projects in relative terms, while the composition of what remains narrows to a few strategic sectors.
verbatim_quote: The survey said the reduction was smaller than the 16% decline in global industrial greenfield FDI reported by UN Trade and Development.
notes: Corroborates the global industrial greenfield contraction figure. Quote provenance manually verified 12/08/2026 from the live page.
